The paper presents the first experimental realization of birefringent transformation optics (TO) devices.
The devices are based on lithographically defined metal/dielectric waveguides.
The devices can perform different functions for mutually orthogonal polarization states of light.
A Luneburg lens for TM polarized light was demonstrated.
A spatial (directional) filter for TE polarized light was demonstrated.
The wavelength range of the experiments was 480-633 nm.
The resolution of the focusing behavior of the TO devices was almost diffraction-limited, with a spot size of ~0.7λ.
The polarization dependence of the TO devices was strong.
The refractive index of the photoresist used in the experiments was n~1.5.
The thickness of the photoresist patterns used in the experiments varied from 0.1-0.3 μm.
The diameter of the TO devices used in the experiments was 6 μm and 2 μm.
The devices exhibited an approximate semi-classical cloaking Hamiltonian.
The experiments were performed using a near-field scanning optical microscope (NSOM) fiber tip.
The devices were fabricated using a lithography technique.
The waveguide thickness was controlled using adiabatic variations of the waveguide shape.
The effective refractive indices for TM and TE polarized light were calculated using the equations (1) and (2).
